claims.text: The deviation is established on the platform's own recorded distances: actual 40.1 km minus recommended 38.3 km = 1.80 km, which is above the 1.0 km tolerance in POL-RD-22's thresholds, so the trip is not within tolerance and the rider's complaint that the driver took a different route is made out.

The driver-device trace confirms which route was taken: fixes place the vehicle on the Pan-Island Expressway from 23:49:57, on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway from 00:02:27, and back on the East Coast Parkway only at 00:14:27 — the PIE/KPE route the rider describes, not the recommended AYE/MCE route, which is exactly the use POL-RD-22 says the trace is for.

The reroute is not traffic-justified. The LTA advisory retrieved for the recommended AYE segment (Jurong Town Hall Road to MCE) over the trip window records type NONE, with no congestion, incident or closure — and POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only on congestion, an incident or a closure.

The driver's explanation that 'night time PIE is faster, no difference much' is an unsupported assertion. POL-RD-23 says in terms that a driver's assertion of traffic with no such data does not justify the reroute, and the only traffic data in the record shows no incident, roadwork or closure on the recommended route and speed bands 6-8 throughout.

The driver gave no notice of the deviation. POL-RD-21 requires the driver to inform the rider by in-app chat, or verbally with a call recording as evidence, before or at the point of deviation; the chat log is a complete, untruncated log with 0 messages, the trip record's in_app_calls is empty, and no recording exists, so the deviation was neither notified nor agreed.

Not traffic-justified and over 1 km puts this case in row (d) of POL-RD-24: the rider is entitled to the excess distance fare in full, being 1.80 km x the base per-km rate of 0.92 SGD = 1.66 SGD without surge, as the fare ledger's own computation shows.

The deviation limb is one the AI can determine on this record: at 1.80 km it is within POL-RD-25's 2 km limit, so the deviation question is not an open question requiring escalation under POL-GEN-26 — the distance is recorded, the route taken is traced, the traffic data is present and the chat log is complete.

The rider is currently carrying the whole charge: the fare ledger shows 90.99 SGD CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd of 0.00, so under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION would simply preserve the present payment state against a rider who has already paid, and on a filed-by-RIDER dispute that is the outcome most adverse to the rider.

To the extent the rider asks for more than the 1.66 SGD that POL-RD-24 provides — 'the fare was far more than I expected', where the fare ledger records a surge amount of 40.04 SGD at a multiplier of 1.8 — the contested amount of 90.99 SGD is above POL-GEN-22's 50.00 SGD ceiling for an AI ruling, so that balance must go before a human reviewer rather than be dismissed.

The fare and surge element of the rider's complaint is a Section 3 matter that POL-GEN-24 does not permit the AI to adjudicate: the rider's demand for the whole 90.99 SGD charge turns on the metered fare and the 1.8x surge in the ledger, which must be routed to human review with the governing v2.1 section named, not disposed of by an AI ruling.

claims.text: The rider asks for the entire 90.99 SGD fare back, but no row of the POL-RD-24 matrix returns a whole trip fare: the most the matrix ever moves is the excess distance fare. Measured the way POL-RD-22 requires — the platform's own recorded distances, actual 40.1 km less recommended 38.3 km = 1.80 km deviation (the 79-fix trace measures only 33.934 km and is expressly not used to re-measure, because a sparse trace understates a route's length) — and priced at the base per-km rate of 0.92 SGD with no surge, the excess distance fare is 1.66 SGD. A full refund of the fare is unsupported by the matrix on its face.

The reason the fare reads high is not the route but the pricing: of the 90.99 SGD charged, 40.04 SGD is surge_amount at a 1.8x multiplier, and the deviation remedy is computed without surge (POL-RD-24 and the category's excess_distance_fare constant, surge_applied false). The rider's complaint that the fare was 'far more than I expected' is a late-night demand-pricing effect; on the fare ledger the itemised excess attributable to the 1.80 km deviation is 1.66 SGD, and the ride's distance and time fares for the route actually driven are not something the deviation matrix returns.

The case cannot be placed in matrix rows (a) or (b), the only rows that turn on traffic justification, because that justification is not in the record: the LTA advisory for the AYE segment towards the city ('Jurong Town Hall Road to MCE') overlaps the trip window (valid 23:17:57 to 00:57:57) but carries advisory_type NONE — 'no incident, roadwork or closure recorded', speed bands 6-8 throughout — and its derived justifies_reroute is false. POL-RD-23 requires congestion, an incident or a closure on the recommended segment, and the driver's own assertion ('night time PIE is faster, no difference much') does not supply the data POL-RD-23 demands. The case therefore falls to row (d): not traffic-justified, deviation over 1 km, which refunds the excess distance fare in full and nothing else.

The rider filed this dispute and the charge still stands: payment_status is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.0. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative and preserves the present payment state, so as to the 89.33 SGD of the fare that is not the excess distance fare, no clause of the route-deviation policy moves it and the present state stands; only 1.66 SGD moves. The rider's claim for the whole fare should be rejected to that extent.

The deviation on this trip is 1.80 km, at or under the 2.0 km limit POL-RD-25 sets for the category, so the route-deviation policy's own escalation trigger is not engaged: this is a rule-bound case whose monetary exposure is fixed by the POL-RD-24 matrix at the excess distance fare, not a case whose deviation size puts it beyond an AI ruling. On that limb the applicable ceiling of 1.66 SGD stands.

Neither party's profile carries fraud_flags of 1 or more — the rider's and the driver's both read 0 — so POL-GEN-22's 0.95 confidence uplift does not apply, and the ordinary threshold for this value band governs how much confidence a ruling on this trip needs. This field is cited only for the confidence test POL-GEN-22 names it for and decides nothing about the trip.

The driver's prior_deviation_flags (1) and deviation_flags_90d (1) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and may never establish a fact about THIS trip or decide it; the same is true of the rider's deviation_claims_60d. The deviation here rests solely on the recorded distances in the trip record (40.1 km actual against 38.3 km recommended), and the driver's history cannot enlarge the remedy beyond the excess distance fare the matrix allows.

The driver gave the rider no in-app chat notice of the change of route — the platform chat log holds 0 entries and matches trip_record.chat_message_count of 0, and the trip record's messages_during_trip list is empty — and POL-RD-21 makes a brief reason enough only where chat or a call recording carries it. That limb is not established, but it is immaterial to the remedy here: rows (b) and (d) of POL-RD-24 pay the same figure, the excess distance fare, so the absence of notice does not increase what the driver owes beyond 1.66 SGD.
